coverage: since the afternoon brief (~13:00–19:30 Berlin); X Following feed back to ~14:15 Berlin
headline: Stolen keys for eight eMudhra certificate authorities force emergency browser blocks; Kyiv and Washington trade blame around the Oslo talks; ByteDance, Alibaba and Tencent order $35bn of Nvidia cards; a ministry typo brings Germany's tobacco tax forward by accident.

stories.title: Private keys for eight eMudhra certificate authorities leak, and browsers block them
facts: The private keys of eight eMudhra intermediate CAs were compromised; they chain to roots trusted by Mozilla, Microsoft, Apple and Chrome.
Anyone holding one of the keys could issue valid-looking HTTPS certificates and impersonate any website to users whose traffic they can intercept.
The reporter proved it by signing a message with each key and reported it to the root programs on Oct 17.
Mozilla blocked the certificates via OneCRL within 3 hours; Chrome also blocked them Oct 17, Apple on Oct 19 and Microsoft on Oct 20.
Mozilla today ships Firefox 158.0.1, ESR 115.43.1 and 153.5.1, and NSS 3.131.1 removes the root that signed the intermediates.
Downstream trust stores were told on Oct 19; many have shipped updates or are still rolling them out.
stories.whyItMatters: Browsers are covered, but tools with their own CA bundles (containers, language runtimes, appliances) only get the fix once their trust store updates.

stories.title: Zelensky meets Witkoff in Oslo while Rubio calls Kyiv's charges "scandalous"
facts: Rubio rejected as "scandalous" the claim that Ukrainians are dying because the US is holding back intelligence, saying nothing is being deliberately denied.
He did concede that Patriot interceptors may not have arrived yet; Kyiv also complains about missing missile warnings and Starshield speed limits.
Zelensky adviser Serhii Beskrestnov told the BBC that unreliable US warnings about ballistic launches are costing lives.
In Oslo Zelensky met Witkoff in person with Kushner on video, hosted by Norway's Støre and Finland's Stubb; Witkoff was not expected at the press conference.
The Kremlin hopes to meet Witkoff soon; AP says a new Russian aerial barrage killed 9 people in Ukraine.
stories.whyItMatters: Material update to the afternoon card: the US is no longer just silent on the missile holdup but publicly disputing Kyiv's account of it.

stories.title: ByteDance, Alibaba and Tencent order more than $35bn of Nvidia's export-compliant cards
facts: Reuters: the three ordered more than 3 million RTX PRO 5500 workstation cards at about $11,400 each.
Nvidia has told partners it can't guarantee delivery; one source says buyers may get only 5–10% of what they asked for.
Another source says Nvidia can make at most 3 million of the cards worldwide in 2027, while total orders from China exceed 6 million.
Samples are due in December and commercial deliveries in Q1 2027; the buyers mainly want them for inference.
B300 sales to China are banned and H200 exports are reviewed case by case, so this card is among the strongest Nvidia parts China can still buy.

stories.title: AfD mail leak: first findings, and a question about voter-register data
facts: taz: the 281 GB dump runs from 2014 to this autumn and includes mails from Weidel, von Storch, Meuthen and Gauland.
The leak site summarized about 39,000 mails, apparently with AI, and flags 611 as "critical" (possible crimes) and 10,450 as "high" relevance.
Lilith Wittmann says after a first look she believes the data is genuine.
The supposed hackers told International Cyber Digest they could have destroyed the servers and turned down money to take the site offline (their claim, unverified).
Wittmann on X: the leak should reopen the debate on why parties can buy targeted registry data for 5 cents per record.
stories.whyItMatters: Follow-up to the afternoon lead: reporting has moved from whether the leak is real to what is in it.

stories.title: A typo in the law gazette would have made Germany's tobacco tax hike start tomorrow
facts: The amendment published in the Federal Law Gazette on Oct 20 says it takes effect "the day after promulgation", which is Oct 21.
That would apply rates meant for 2030 straight away; the industry says no matching tax stamps exist, so it would have had to stop deliveries.
The finance ministry admits a "technical error": the higher rates are meant to apply from Jan 1, 2027, and a correction is underway.
Factories may keep delivering, the ministry says; a pack of 20 is expected to rise by about €4 to €11.78 by 2030.

stories.title: Oil hits a five-month high, then slips on a peace-plan report; the DAX ends flat
facts: Brent topped $111 in the morning after Iran repeated its claim to control the Strait of Hormuz, then fell to about $108.65.
The trigger was a report that Qatari and Pakistani mediators sent Iran and the US a new peace proposal that both received positively.
The DAX recovered from near 25,000 to close at 25,304 (−0.06%); the CAC 40 lost 0.4% on the French unrest.
German producer prices jumped 1.9% on the month and 6.7% on the year; the ZEW index fell 6.6 points to 28.1.
CNBC: the Dow was up about 400 points on solid earnings and lower crude; SAP reports on Wednesday.

stories.title: Anthropic: Claude designed proteins that bind scorpion neurotoxins
facts: An internal research Claude model designed minibinders (small proteins that latch onto a target) against scorpion neurotoxins.
It worked from one prompt plus four follow-ups, written with Citrini Research to test whether motivated non-experts could tackle a real health problem.
Adaptyv Bio and Twist Bioscience lab-tested 211 designs; 17 met Anthropic's binding criteria.
Anthropic is releasing all 211 designs and their data; scorpions sting about 1.2 million people a year and antivenoms are often scarce.

facts.text: Google blames a "power event" at London data centres for the europe-west2 outage; service was back for most customers by about 15:00 UK time.
Revolut's iDEAL/Wero disruption in the Netherlands was marked resolved at 14:56 UTC after more than 7.5 hours.
VW is recalling more than 70,000 electric cars worldwide to check potentially faulty batteries, shortly after its big screw recall.
Sudan: army drones hit mourners and a fuel market, killing more than 200 people, sources tell the BBC.
UK police re-arrested two men on suspicion of assisting Iranian intelligence after an incident at RAF Fairford.
Romania's parliament elected nonpartisan diplomat Luca Niculescu prime minister after months without a working government.
GitHub package firewall (public preview) checks npm package metadata and downloads for malware before they reach CI/CD hosts or coding agents.
Cloudflare is collaborating on tsrs, a Rust port of TypeScript it says is up to 8x faster and uses 70% less memory.
Mistral Voxtral 3: new speech-to-text and text-to-speech models for 50+ languages plus a voice-agent SDK, via EU-hosted API or self-hosting.
Svelte merges a fix that skips redundant attribute writes during hydration.
Node.js's Matteo Collina says he failed Anthropic's Cyber Verification Program because Node.js has no Claude company account.
swyx quotes DeepSeek's Zhihu post: one V4.1 Flash cluster serves 155 trillion tokens a day at $38 revenue per card-hour (off-peak prices).
